Your files exactly as stored, at their own sample rate and bit depth. About 0.4 GB an hour for CD-quality FLAC, more for hi-res.
The quality for songs streamed over mobile data. A song already playing, or fetched ahead, plays as it is.
Uses the ReplayGain tags in your files so quiet and loud tracks play at a similar level.
How loud that level is. Loud can round off the peaks of dynamic music; Normal and Quiet never do.
Song makes every song equally loud. Album keeps an album\'s quiet and loud songs in proportion. Auto uses Album while you play an album through in order, and Song for playlists and shuffle.
Songs with nothing to go by

Levelling goes by a tag in each file that says how much to turn the song down. A song without one is treated as if its tag said this much, which is about what most do, so it doesn\'t stand out louder than the rest.

resources.string: “Everything” goes by your server\'s count of each song\'s plays, which takes in every app you\'ve listened with. The shorter stretches of time, and the playlists, go by the plays Nexus Music itself has counted, which start on %1$s.

Ask for music that isn\'t in your library

For people who run Lidarr beside their music server. Search gains a “Not in your library” section; asking for something there puts it on Lidarr\'s list, and the Requests page shows what\'s on its way. Songs and track lists are looked up at MusicBrainz, which is sent what you search for. How much each is played comes from ListenBrainz, which is told which artists and songs came up.

A song that never came out on an album is offered on its single or EP, and artists\' pages list those as well. Asking for one has Lidarr list that artist\'s singles and EPs alongside their albums; only what you ask for is fetched.
